Amgen’s profile is **a large, cash-generative biotech with several growing newer products—but also meaningful patent, pricing and pipeline risks**.

### Strengths
- **Scale and financial strength.** In 2025, Amgen reported $36.8 billion in revenue, up 10%, and $8.1 billion in free cash flow. It invested $7.3 billion in R&D. [Amgen’s 2025 shareholder letter](turn1view2)
- **A broad portfolio with multiple growth engines.** Fourteen products each generated more than $1 billion in 2025 sales. Fast-growing examples included Repatha, for cardiovascular risk, and the osteoporosis drug Evenity; the rare-disease portfolio also grew. [Amgen’s 2025 results](turn1view2)
- **Promising newer products and pipeline options.** In Q2 2026, Amgen said six key growth drivers grew 26% year over year and made up nearly 70% of product sales. MariTide, its investigational obesity treatment, is in Phase 3 trials—though it remains unproven commercially. [Q2 2026 results](turn1view0) [MariTide update](turn1view0)
- **Strong cash generation and shareholder returns.** Amgen has the resources to fund research, manufacturing investment and dividends. Its 2025 letter reported 14 consecutive years of dividend growth. [2025 shareholder letter](turn1view2)

### Weaknesses and risks
- **Patent expirations and biosimilar erosion.** Amgen’s own filing warns that biosimilars can intensify price competition. This is already visible in Prolia and Xgeva: in Q2 2026, their sales were down 32% and 34%, respectively, year over year, with the company citing biosimilar competition. [10-K competition discussion](turn1view1) [Q2 2026 product results](turn1view0)
- **Dependence on continued product launches and R&D success.** New indications and pipeline medicines may help offset older-product declines, but clinical trials can fail, and competing treatments may win market share. Amgen’s filing identifies development and competition as business risks. [Amgen 10-K](turn1view1)
- **Pricing and reimbursement pressure.** Government policy, Medicare drug-price provisions and payer negotiations can limit prices or access. Amgen flags these as risks to sales and profitability in its 10-K. [Amgen 10-K](turn1view1)
- **Substantial debt.** As of June 30, 2026, Amgen reported $57.3 billion of debt and $14.0 billion in cash. Strong cash flow helps, but the debt load can constrain flexibility. [Q2 2026 balance sheet](turn1view3)
- **Manufacturing concentration.** Amgen says most of its commercial manufacturing is at a Puerto Rico facility, leaving supply exposed to disruptions there; it also highlights concentration of clinical manufacturing in California. [Amgen 10-K](turn1view1)

**Bottom line:** Amgen’s main advantage is its scale, cash generation and ability to grow newer medicines across several disease areas. The key question is whether those growth drivers can keep expanding fast enough to offset biosimilar losses and pricing pressure.

### Main strengths
- **Scale and cash generation:** In 2025, revenue rose 10% to **$36.8 billion** and free cash flow was **$8.1 billion**. Amgen reported 18 products with record sales and 14 with more than $1 billion in annual sales. ([2025 shareholder letter](https://www.amgen.com/stories/2026/03/2025-letter-to-shareholders))
- **Several products are growing quickly:** Repatha and EVENITY each grew strongly in 2025; rare-disease medicines and TEZSPIRE also added growth. ([Q2 2026 results](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/318154/000031815426000124/amgn-20260630earningsrelea.htm))
- **Research and development investment:** Amgen spent about **$7.3 billion on R&D in 2025**. Its obesity candidate MariTide is in Phase 3 trials, offering potential upside if it proves safe and effective and can compete commercially. ([2025 shareholder letter](https://www.amgen.com/stories/2026/03/2025-letter-to-shareholders))
- **Broad commercial and therapeutic experience:** The company sells medicines across areas including cancer, inflammation, cardiovascular disease and rare disease, and has experience developing and selling both original biologic medicines and biosimilars.

### Main weaknesses and risks
- **Biosimilar competition is already cutting sales:** Prolia sales fell **32%** and XGEVA sales fell **34%** year over year in Q2 2026, as biosimilars entered the market. Amgen’s 10-K warns that competition often intensifies as more biosimilars launch. ([Q2 2026 results](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/318154/000031815426000124/amgn-20260630earningsrelea.htm); [2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/318154/000031815426000010/amgn-20251231.htm))
- **Pricing and reimbursement pressure:** Government programs, insurers and pharmacy-benefit managers can constrain prices or coverage. Amgen’s 10-K specifically flags drug-pricing policies and payer pressure as risks to sales and profitability. ([2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/318154/000031815426000010/amgn-20251231.htm))
- **Pipeline outcomes are uncertain:** MariTide and other clinical candidates could fail trials, face delays or prove less commercially attractive than hoped. Amgen is investing heavily, but R&D spending does not guarantee successful launches.
- **Substantial debt:** At June 30, 2026, Amgen reported **$57.3 billion in debt** and $14.0 billion in cash. Strong cash generation helps, but the debt load can limit flexibility and makes interest costs relevant. ([Q2 2026 results](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/318154/000031815426000124/amgn-20260630earningsrelea.htm))
- **Manufacturing concentration:** The company says most of its commercial manufacturing is at a Puerto Rico facility, leaving supply more exposed to a major disruption there. ([2025 Form 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/318154/000031815426000010/amgn-20251231.htm))

**Bottom line:** Amgen’s core strengths are its established portfolio, cash generation and growing newer products. The key question is whether those growth drivers can keep expanding fast enough to offset biosimilar losses and pricing pressure—while the pipeline, including MariTide, remains a risk rather than a guaranteed replacement.
